sections.overview: The Silver-rumped Spinetail is a small swift of the family Apodidae, resident in parts of South-East Asia.
sections.identification: It is dark-plumaged with a conspicuous pale, silvery-white rump and upper tail-coverts.
sections.habitat: It is often seen flying above lowland forest and its edges, including clearings and riverside openings.
sections.diet: It catches flying insects in the air.
sections.behavior: A study describes it roosting in large tree hollows high in the canopy and documents flexible energy-saving temperature regulation.
sections.reproduction: The field guide gives general needletail breeding figures, not confirmed species-specific measurements.
sections.ecology: The two common English names, Silver-rumped Spinetail and Silver-rumped Needletail, refer to the same swift.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern; the population trend is reported as stable.
